text:
sarah-customer-support: FYI we have a high-severity from ACME (acct acme-prod). Customers seeing intermittent 504s + p95 spikes to ~12s starting ~09:10 UTC. Ticket #12345 opened. Sample request_id: req_89b2fc. Can we triage?

alex-eng: Thanks Sarah. Any idea which endpoint/model? payload sizes?

sarah-customer-support: It's /v1/generate (hosted). Model is redwood/opt-8b (verified in account). Typical input tokens ~120, but we have some long inputs ~2000 tokens from a single tenant.

maya-ops: Looking at infra metrics — ingress_queue_depth for the cluster spiked to 1.15k at 09:12. Our soft limit is 1000, hard reject at 1500. Continuous-batcher backlog latency also climbed; batch wait time p99 ~340ms -> 900ms. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/ingress/queue?id=acme-prod (shared privately).

jordan-ml: Long sequences can cause longer generation times so they occupy execution lanes longer; if batching window increases, tail latency worsens. Do we have KV cache churn for that tenant?

samir-eng: I see a pattern in gateway logs: many requests held in request-queue until batcher available, then some timeouts fired in gateway with 504. Snippet: ```ERROR gateway: request req_89b2fc timeout after 30s waiting in queue depth=1147```. That's consistent with queue saturation.

ops-bot: autoscaler: no scaling event triggered between 09:00-09:20 — reason: node pool reached AZ instance quota.

alex-eng: Actionable items: 1) repro locally with a mix of long/short seq to reproduce backlog; 2) consider temporary mitigation: lower max_batch_wait_ms to reduce queueing, enable early-reject on requests exceeding max_queue_wait_ms; 3) check tenant throttles and per-tenant queue caps.

sarah-customer-support: Customer impact: several users timed out and reported degraded UX; they want ETA. I told them we're investigating and will provide mitigation.

maya-ops: Quick mitigation applied: bumped per-cluster ingress_queue_soft_limit from 1000 -> 1400 and enabled early_reject_threshold=1200 for this cluster. Also raised alerting sensitivity. Observed immediate drop in pending queue from 1150 -> 820 within 2m.

jordan-ml: Long-term: consider adaptive batch sizing to reduce tail; also suggest rejecting extremely long inputs at gateway or route them to non-shared Dedicated capacity.

samir-eng: Repro steps I used: 
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood/opt-8b","input":"<2000 tokens>","max_tokens":800}' 
2) fire 200 concurrent mixed-length requests over 2 minutes (short: ~100 tokens, long: ~1800 tokens)
Expected: queue_depth climbs, some gateway timeouts at our current soft limits.

alex-eng: Diagnostic checklist: 
- Check request_queue_depth and continuous_batch_wait_ms around incident window.
- Verify batcher thread counts and GPU utilization (if high, indicates processing bottleneck).
- Inspect autoscaler logs for AZ quota or instance failures.
- Dump gateway request queue for top tenants by queued time.

ops-bot: Note: spot-instance interruption events at 09:05 in us-west-2 contributed to temporary capacity shortfall. Autoscaler attempted replacement but hit AZ quota until 09:14.

maya-ops: Follow-up: scheduled a capacity bump for the cluster and submitted AZ quota request. Also created a temporary route rule to send tenant acme-prod's long-seq traffic to a dedicated pool for next 24h.

sarah-customer-support: Communicated mitigation to customer; they accepted dedicated routing as short-term solution. They want permanent fixes.

alex-eng: Recommended permanent changes: 
- Implement per-tenant queue caps (protect shared pool)
- Add early-reject for requests exceeding max_queue_wait_ms + clearer 429 semantics for overload
- Adaptive batching and per-request timeout propagation to avoid holding queue slots for long-running requests
- Runbook updates: include spot/quotas checks and immediate switch to dedicated routing when queue_depth > 1k sustained for 3m.

samir-eng: I'll open a follow-up PR to add per-tenant cap and a config toggle for early-reject.

jordan-ml: I'll prototype adaptive batch window and evaluate impact in canary.

maya-ops: I'll post incident postmortem tomorrow with graphs and timeline. For now metrics back to normal and customer confirming improved behavior. :white_check_mark:

alex-eng: Summary: root cause = request queue saturation due to mix of extreme long-sequence requests + capacity shortfall (spot interruptions + AZ quota). Short-term mitigations applied (bump soft-limit, early_reject, dedicated routing). Long-term action items assigned. Closing thread once postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
